description: Somos un grupo de amigos interesados en el código y desarrollo web, por otro lado también nos apasiona el deporte, decidimos entrar a este concurso porque estamos seguros que tenemos las herramientas para desarrollarnos de una manera correcta y ganar
summary: DARKSIDE is a 3D computer game built with the Godot Engine where players design a spacecraft and fly it to the Moon. We noticed that there is no quick, simple, and realistic way to try a Moon mission that also teaches, so we made one for the Space Mission Design Game challenge. Before launch, players spend a limited budget of 150 credits and a mass limit on solar panels, shielding, an engine, a science instrument, an antenna, a launcher, and a route. Every part adds cost and mass, so each choice is a trade-off. During the flight, live NASA data changes how hard the trip is: near-Earth asteroids from NeoWs, solar flares from DONKI, and the distance to the Moon from JPL Horizons. NASA 3D models appear in the launch and landing cinematics. The project matters because students learn in minutes that a Moon mission is a chain of decisions and that space weather is a real risk.
details:
What it does: DARKSIDE: Mission to the Moon is a 3D game made with the Godot Engine. The player designs a spacecraft, launches it, flies it to the Moon, lands, and reads a mission report.

How it works: In the design screen the player has 150 credits and a mass limit to spend on solar panels, shielding, an engine, a science instrument, an antenna, a launcher, and a route. Every part adds cost and mass, so each choice is a trade-off between speed, safety, and science. Then comes a cinematic launch, the flight, and the landing.

NASA data: The game downloads live data. Near-Earth asteroids from the NASA NeoWs API set how many asteroids appear on the route. Solar flares from NASA DONKI set the space-weather danger level. The Earth-Moon distance from JPL Horizons sets the trip length. Data is cached on the device. NASA 3D models and images are used in the launch and landing cinematics and the scenery.

Benefits and impact: Students learn in a few minutes that a Moon mission is a chain of decisions and that space weather is a real risk. It also shows how free NASA data can power creative tools. It runs on a regular PC and was built by high-school students in the Dominican Republic.

Creativity: We found no fast, free digital game that mixes mission design with live NASA data and realistic limits, so we built one. The ship you design changes how the flight plays out.

Tools: Godot Engine 4 (GDScript), NASA open APIs, NASA 3D resources, Canva for the demo slides.

How to play: Windows only. Download the ZIP, extract it, and run CEQUISAspace.exe. If Windows SmartScreen appears, click More info, then Run anyway.

AI use: We used Claude (Anthropic) to help write and debug code, to write the code that generates the sound effects and music, to port the cinematics, and to draft the demo slides and this form. The team directed and reviewed all work. We did not use AI to make images, video, or audio files.
